title: Scoped thresholds: what a coverage-law change must deliver for the selected complex local word (no new kappa)
body:
**Status: scoped obstruction + exact threshold table under the optimistic relaxation. No new κ; the selected record is unchanged.** Contributor: **Navinor**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

Adds only `research/complex-coverage-law-relief/`. `upstream/`, frozen pins and the selected record are untouched.

## Task card
- **Card:** `complex-new-helper-inventory` (complex-mechanisms, chooser track, OS-random nonce `6ddf1b6647d8c5131033b16d30f0045b`, base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`, priority revision 2). Scope is **refined** to the card's first experiment (the complete optimistic child histogram, rejecting routes without headroom), applied to **changed coverage-law interfaces** instead of a new contract; reason is recorded in `TASK.json`/`TASK-CARD.md`.
- **Question:** with the selected [PR 1094](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094) local word fixed (`{1:2412, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8}`, mass 5586 per call; coverage law `m = 73`, `w = 896/9` families per call, centre 64, unpaid 1, idle rank cap 51), which interface changes are necessary and which sufficient for the optimistic moment to reach `a = 1/99` (κ = 0.01) or the retained-transfer unbinding saving `a = κ_bit/(1−κ_bit) = 0.001736437026484097`?

## Result (all brackets certified, exact rational intervals, code-disjoint from [PR 1240](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240))
Positive control: `a* = 0.001690054109088696` reproduces https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240's grid ceiling `a < 0.001690054109089` within one 1e-15 step. The incumbent ceiling is **below the unbinding target**, so pure repacking cannot unbind the complex side; an interface change is required even for the near target.

| Lever (others at the selected line) | T2: unbinding | T1: `a = 1/99` |
|---|---|---|
| unpaid coordinates per family `u` | `u* ∈ (1.009826689, 1.009826689)`, least integer 2 | `u* ∈ (2.804078009, 2.804078010)`, least integer 3 |
| centre charge `c` (from 64) | `c* ∈ (63.021698514, 63.021698515)` | **impossible**: sup `a* = 0.004711142955614` at `c = 0` |
| families per replica `F` (9 stages) | least met 906 (905 fails) | least met 3093 (3092 fails) |
| paid-word count scale `s` | met iff `s ≤ 0.969437086` | met iff `s ≤ 0.049110034` |

Pair points at `F = 896`: `(u=2, c=0)` gives `a* = 0.009357801683738 < 1/99` — unpaid relief up to 2 with **any** centre charge fails T1 (sup over `c` is at `c = 0`); `(u=3, c=64)` gives `a* = 0.011001994530886 > 1/99` (optimistic sufficiency). The 4.911% word-scaling threshold independently matches https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240's "about 95% lower fully priced local excess spend". The `a* < D/E` diagnostic inequality is certified at four points (incumbent `D/E = 0.001695287130359` vs `a* = 0.001690054109089`).

## Not covered / limitations
- Necessity holds inside the stated model only; sufficiency is optimistic-relaxation (fractional counts, all idle at rank ≤ 51, no added charges). **No physical realizability, owner map, finite invoice, cold replay or new kappa.** The card's acceptance gate (a new physically realizable contract) is not met by this PR.
- `u`, `c` and the pair points are at `F = 896`; `F`, `s` at `u = 1, c = 64`. `u > 1`, `c ≠ 64` are what-if coverage laws needing their own admission. `κ = a/(1+a)` is the retained planning transfer; T2 uses the bit supplier pinned at the base commit.
- Inherited all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic-transfer and bit H1–H5 assumptions remain.

## Overlap / credit
- [PR 1012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012)'s coverage identity; https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240 (Douglas Colkitt) for the moment model and fixed-word ceiling; https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1264 for the 14-claim census at the unchanged law. The pending `levers.py` ideal-budget table referenced by https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1272's proposed `centre-path-sharing`/`coverage-law-change` cards is complementary: this PR certifies exact threshold brackets (not first-order multiples), adds the families and word-scaling levers, least-integer thresholds, the pair obstruction and convexity margins, on the base commit.
- Ali Romman's `research/heterogeneous-owner-assembly/` bounds the frozen catalogue's 25 cost interfaces and excludes new helper-inventory interfaces (the R489/R480 interfaces of [PR 1004](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1004) and [PR 1005](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1005)); these thresholds price what such a new interface must deliver.
- Distinct from https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1265 (idle repartitions at a fixed law) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1315 (X2 owner-map acceptance boundary). Claim thread: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1328.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-coverage-law-relief/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-coverage-law-relief --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-coverage-law-relief
```
Expected final line `PASS_COMPLEX_COVERAGE_LAW_RELIEF` (23 PASS checks: coverage identity, the [PR 1240](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240) ceiling reproduction, threshold brackets, pair points, four D/E margins, six failure/monotonicity controls). Also ran `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'`: 14 pass; the 6 `test_research_onboarding.PackageTests` errors are pre-existing on this Windows machine at the pristine base commit (verified with my changes stashed) and unrelated to this package.

**Credit:** all construction credit for the selected local word stays with its authors (see `certificates/selected-result.json` and `research/gauge44-slots-t16/README.md`). Prepared by Navinor with substantial opencode assistance. No human review or full formal verification is claimed.
